**Nephritic vs Nephrotic Syndrome** ★★ — Inflammation + RBC casts + HTN + proteinuria ==<3.5 g/day== (nephritic) vs podocyte effacement + fatty casts + hypoalbuminaemia ==<3.0 g/dL== + proteinuria ==≥3.5 g/day== (nephrotic).

## Discrimination (vs)

| Feature | Nephritic syndrome ★★ | Nephrotic syndrome ★★ |
|---|---|---|
| **Lesion** | Glomerular inflammation (GBM damage) | Podocyte foot-process effacement (==without== prominent inflammation) |
| **Proteinuria** ★★ | ==<3.5 g/day== | ==≥3.5 g/day== (UPCR ≥3.5 g/g), frothy urine |
| **Urine sediment** ★★ | Dysmorphic RBCs (acanthocytes), **RBC casts**, cola urine | **Fatty casts**, oval fat bodies, **Maltese crosses**, ==without RBC casts== |
| **BP / GFR / Oedema** | **Hypertension**, oliguria, azotaemia, mild periorbital oedema | Severe **hypoalbuminaemia ==<3.0 g/dL==**, anasarca |
| **Major complications** | Rapid renal failure (RPGN crescents) | **Hyperlipidaemia**, **thrombosis** (AT-III loss → renal vein thrombosis, esp. membranous), **encapsulated infections** (Ig loss, *S. pneumoniae*) |
| **Prototypes** | **PSGN** (==2-4 weeks==, ↓C3, subepithelial humps), **IgA** (==1-3 days==, normal C3), **RPGN** (crescents) | **Minimal change** (children, steroid-responsive), **FSGS** (adults of African ancestry), **Membranous** (anti-PLA2R, spike-and-dome) |

## Mnemonic (Nephritic — **PHARAOH**)

- **P** — Proteinuria (==<3.5 g/day==)
- **H** — Haematuria (dysmorphic RBCs / acanthocytes)
- **A** — Azotaemia (↑BUN/Cr)
- **R** — RBC casts
- **A** — ASO / ↓complement (in PSGN)
- **O** — Oliguria
- **H** — Hypertension

## Buzzword →

- **Cola-coloured urine + RBC casts** → nephritic syndrome
- **Maltese crosses + fatty casts** → nephrotic syndrome
- **Synpharyngitic haematuria (1-3 days), normal C3** → IgA nephropathy
- **2-4 weeks post-infection, low C3, subepithelial humps** → PSGN
- **Anti-PLA2R + renal vein thrombosis** → membranous nephropathy

## ⚠ Never

- ==Do not diagnose nephrotic syndrome on dipstick alone== ==without quantifying proteinuria ≥3.5 g/day==.
- ==Do not overlook overlap syndromes== — MPGN and diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis can present with **both** nephritic and nephrotic features simultaneously.

## Cards

- Proteinuria cut-off separating nephritic from nephrotic syndrome → Nephritic <3.5 g/day; nephrotic ≥3.5 g/day (UPCR ≥3.5 g/g)
- Urine microscopy findings in nephritic vs nephrotic syndrome → Nephritic: dysmorphic RBCs (acanthocytes) and RBC casts; nephrotic: fatty casts, oval fat bodies, and Maltese crosses without RBC casts
- Latency and complement levels distinguishing PSGN from IgA nephropathy → PSGN: 2-4 weeks after infection with low C3; IgA nephropathy: 1-3 days (synpharyngitic) with normal complement
- Why do nephrotic patients develop hypercoagulability and encapsulated bacterial infections? → Urinary loss of antithrombin III (thrombosis, especially renal vein thrombosis in membranous) and immunoglobulins (infection, e.g. S. pneumoniae)
- Can you diagnose nephrotic syndrome from a urine dipstick alone? → No; never diagnose without quantifying proteinuria ≥3.5 g/day
- Which two glomerular diseases classically show mixed nephritic-nephrotic overlap? → Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) and diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis
